It is a matter of profound spiritual gravity to sit with the “unsearchable riches” of Christ while witnessing the “noise and tumult” of a world that seeks to “remodel the way we think about truth” through the “wicked deed” of false accusation, and I must ask you with a gentle spirit: why do you ask after the nature of the false witness and the perversion of justice in this hour? [13, 207, 340, 1198, 1503, 1605, Conversation History]. Are you perhaps feeling “overwhelmed and desperate” by a “spirit of fraud” where men “circulate a false report” to destroy their enemies, or are you seeking a “settled certainty” to anchor your soul in the truth that the Master “sovereignly orders everything He has made”—including the final reckoning for every “lying tongue”? [1, 13, 20, 224, 353, 537, 1143, 1503, 1605, Conversation History]. In a day when many “shave off the edges” of the truth to protect “allies” or “religious leaders” who have “neglected the weightier matters of the law,” we must return to the “external Word” to see how the Lord personally governs the “vicissitudes of life” by demanding that we “ascribe greatness to our God” through absolute honesty [11, 28, 130, 204, 324, 536, 1118, 1503, 1515, Conversation History].

The Reformed tradition teaches that “God personally and exhaustively pervades and sustains and governs every aspect of His creation,” and therefore, the bearing of false witness is not an “administrative anomaly” but an “abomination to the LORD” that strikes at the very character of the “God of truth” [15, 63, 68, 1143, 1191, 1532, 1720, Conversation History].

***

### **Section 1: The Prohibition of the Lie (The Ninth Commandment)**

**Verse**
“ ‘You shall not bear false witness against your neighbor’ ” (Exodus 20:16). [965, 993, 1046, 1117, Conversation History].

**Meaning**
The sources teach that “truth and virtue are well protected” by this command, for any “untruthful testimony” disturbs the “societal stability” and “righteousness” God requires of His people [991, 998, Conversation History]. To “bear false witness” is to “put your hand with the wicked to be an unrighteous witness,” a practice that God “will not at all acquit” (Exodus 23:1; Nahum 1:3) [63, 224, 977, 1006, Conversation History]. Reformed theology—echoed by **John MacArthur**—asserts that this command is not merely an external rule but a reflection of God’s “perfect holiness,” for He is a “God of truth and without injustice” (Leviticus 19:2; Deuteronomy 32:4) [61, 83, 324, 1111, Conversation History].

**Takeaway**
You should “not be deceived” by the “cunning craftiness” of those who think a “cleverly devised myth” can serve a good cause, for “your life is not your own” because you were “bought at a price” (2 Peter 1:16; 1 Corinthians 6:20) [12, 101, 113, 296, 1138, 1262, 1406, 1502, 1670, Conversation History]. Recognize that “lying lips are an abomination to the LORD,” and you must instead “speak truth with [your] neighbor” (Proverbs 12:22; Ephesians 4:25) [770, 771, Conversation History].

**Advanced Note: Judicial Context**
In the ancient **Jewish context**, the “highest religious court,” the Sanhedrin, was ultimately exposed as “riddled with injustice and corruption” when they “devised and carried out the conspiracy” to condemn Christ through “false witnesses” (Matthew 26:59–60) [76, 130, 205, 1316, 1365, 1422, 1720, Conversation History]. The New Testament **revises** our standard by teaching that “love is the fulfilling of the law,” meaning that the believer’s “yes” must simply mean “yes,” for we live under the “perfect law of liberty” (Romans 13:10; James 5:12; James 1:25) [13, 142, 726, 995, 1312, 1313, 1426, 1445, Conversation History].

***

### **Section 2: The Character of the Accuser (Wisdom and Law)**

**Verse**
“ ‘A false witness who speaks lies, and one who sows discord among brethren’ ” (Proverbs 6:19). [353, 537, 634, Conversation History].

**Meaning**
The “record of history” reveals that God “hates” the “lying tongue” and a “heart that devises wicked plans” because such things are “abominable to Him” (Proverbs 6:16–18) [11, 15, 353, 537, 634, 1143, 1532, 1720, Conversation History]. Scripture handles the “clamor and tumult” of accusations by requiring that “by the mouth of two or three witnesses every word may be established,” ensuring that “no partiality” or “bribes” pervert the verdict (Deuteronomy 19:15; Matthew 18:16) [301, 501, 848, 858, 871, 1006, 1317, Conversation History]. A false accuser is described as a “fowler’s snare” who “strengthen[s] the hands of evil doers,” leading the people into “futility” (Hosea 9:8; Jeremiah 23:14, 25) [24, 25, 1264, Conversation History].

**Takeaway**
“Trade in your worry for trust,” for the Lord is the “Judge of all the earth” who “will surely hear their cry” when the innocent are “unjustly accused” (Genesis 18:25; Exodus 22:23) [83, 94, 201, 222, 501, 909, 1012, 1408, 1515, Conversation History]. You must “discipline your mind” to “not follow a crowd to do evil,” refusing to “testify in a dispute so as to... pervert justice” simply because a majority demands it (Exodus 23:2) [90, 116, 224, 977, 1006, 1406, 1515, 1709, Conversation History].

**Advanced Note: Foreordained Vengeance**
Under the **Mosaic Law**, God commanded that the community “shall do to [the false witness] as he thought to have done to his brother,” a strict “eye for eye” penalty intended to “put away the evil from among you” (Deuteronomy 19:19, 21; Exodus 21:24) [217, 291, 294, 301, 872, 970, 1001, 1098, Conversation History]. The New Testament **revises** our “warfare,” teaching that while “vengeance is Mine, I will repay,” we must “love your enemies” and “pray for those who spitefully use you” (Romans 12:19; Matthew 5:44) [13, 21, 28, 32, 43, 51, 92, 125, 202, 372, 461, 1023, 1081, 1313, 1326, 1426, 1515, 1529, 1646, 1670, Conversation History].

***

### **Section 3: The Sin of Partiality (Allies vs. Enemies)**

**Verse**
“ ‘My brethren, do not hold the faith of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Lord of glory, with partiality. . . . If you show partiality, you commit sin, and are convicted by the law as transgressors’ ” (James 2:1, 9). [111, 542, Conversation History].

**Meaning**
The Reformed tradition—echoed by **Paul Washer**—teaches that “God shows no partiality,” and therefore the church must not “become judges with evil motives” by applying moral standards selectively [111, 542, Conversation History]. Human beings often “justify themselves before men” while being “stunningly oblivious” to their own “hardness of heart,” treating the sins of allies with “kid gloves” while “declaim[ing] passionately against the visible sins of others” (Luke 16:15; Matthew 12:34) [36, 49, 57, 58, 71, 77, 218, 1267, 1269, 1430, 1551, Conversation History]. To condemn what you have not “examined” is to “judge according to appearance” rather than “righteous judgment,” making one a “spirit of fraud” who “muffles the truth” (John 7:24) [11, 37, 38, 1269, 1270, 1483, 1503, Conversation History].

**Takeaway**
“Your life is not your own,” and your “sole objective” is to “adorn the doctrine of God” by “showing all good fidelity” to the truth, regardless of who it implicates (Titus 2:10) [12, 33, 101, 361, 779, 799, 1131, 1138, 1227, 1262, 1406, 1450, 1502, 1670, Conversation History]. You should “not look for some other fountain of knowledge” in “political maneuvering” to justify partiality; instead, “test all things; hold fast what is good” (1 Thessalonians 5:21) [11, 21, 30, 51, 90, 116, 121, 123, 1406, 1408, 1503, 1515, 1709, Conversation History].

**Advanced Note: Continuity of the Decree**
Under the **theocratic context**, judges were warned to “not show partiality in judgment; you shall hear the small as well as the great,” for “the judgment is God’s” (Deuteronomy 1:17) [272, 846, 858, 860, 1041, 1316, 1365, 1473, Conversation History]. The New Testament **revises** our “witness,” showing that because we are “all one in Christ Jesus,” any “unrighteous deception” practiced toward an enemy or for an ally is a denial of the “One who wrote the Word” (Galatians 3:28; 2 Thessalonians 2:10) [13, 26, 32, 136, 142, 167, 176, 440, 1216, 1288, 1313, 1341, 1426, Conversation History].

***

### **Section 4: The LORD as the Sole Sovereign**

**Verse**
“ ‘For the LORD is our Judge, The LORD is our Lawgiver, The LORD is our King; He will save us’ ” (Isaiah 33:22). [594, Conversation History].

**Meaning**
The biblical authors resolve the “noise and tumult” of corrupt legal systems by fixating on the “consummation of history,” where “Christ ultimately crushes the kingdoms of men and establishes His own” [13, 20, 21, 24, 31, 103, 136, 1199, 1315, 1515, 1720, Conversation History]. Because God alone occupies these three offices, no human being or “storage city” of human building can rightfully claim absolute authority to “justify the wicked” or “condemn the just” (Proverbs 17:15) [6, 15, 23, 37, 63, 68, 170, 236, 1143, 1233, 1402, 1532, 1720, Conversation History]. Every ruler who seeks to “write themselves into God’s office” will ultimately be “weighed on the scales and found deficient” (Daniel 5:27) [11, 15, 30, 37, 324, 412, 914, 1061, 1143, 1402, 1450, 1502, 1720, Conversation History].

**Takeaway**
“Wait for His Son from heaven,” knowing that “the Lord knows those who are His” and His “everlasting dominion” is the only kingdom that “shall not pass away” (1 Thessalonians 1:10; 2 Timothy 2:19; Daniel 7:14) [11, 14, 24, 47, 87, 92, 103, 109, 121, 147, 176, 179, 182, 201, 211, 257, 266, 273, 278, 285, 300, 313, 324, 332, 352, 361, 382, 386, 405, 412, 413, 414, 444, 449, 455, 470, 553, 587, 588, 591, 602, 603, 614, 630, 717, 788, 803, 815, 816, 825, 827, 852, 869, 903, 912, 917, 921, 940, 947, 958, 1035, 1113, 1132, 1138, 1143, 1183, 1197, 1203, 1206, 1211, 1218, 1233, 1243, 1251, 1252, 1255, 1257, 1259, 1282, 1300, 1301, 1306, 1311, 1312, 1313, 1315, 1407, 1408, 1420, 1426, 1441, 1450, 1515, 1532, 1572, 1636, 1684, 1720, Conversation History]. Find “tranquility of soul” by resting on the “surest foundation,” for “nothing thwarts any aspect of His plan” (Psalm 138:2; Job 42:2) [5, 11, 21, 30, 92, 121, 147, 176, 178, 201, 313, 318, 352, 412, 602, 630, 957, 1012, 1132, 1143, 1181, 1199, 1214, 1306, 1312, 1315, 1408, 1420, 1450, 1515, 1532, 1572, 1684, 1720, Conversation History].

***

**Final Reminder**
“Nevertheless the firm foundation of God stands, having this seal, ‘The Lord knows those who are His,’ and, ‘Everyone who names the name of the Lord is to abstain from wickedness’ ” (2 Timothy 2:19). [11, 87, 104, 147, 149, 176, 201, 211, 222, 285, 291, 300, 311, 313, 324, 325, 332, 335, 361, 405, 413, 414, 444, 449, 591, 834, 1132, 1138, 1407, 1441, 1450, Conversation History].
